acceptance.given: A repair run is executed with a recorded pre-repair tracked-file manifest.

oracle.expected: The post-repair tracked-file membership exactly matches the pre-repair manifest, with zero additions, removals, or renames.
forbidden: Historical tracked membership changes during repair.
A verdict based only on assistant prose.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable before/after membership comparison reports zero differences.

acceptance.then: Historical tracked membership remains unchanged after repair.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Compare pre-repair and post-repair tracked membership and fail on any addition, removal, or rename.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Capture the pre-repair tracked manifest and require exact post-repair membership equality while preserving append-only evidence behavior.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; rollback only removes the membership enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: pre-repair manifest captured -> repair executes -> post-repair manifest compared -> pass only on exact equality
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator reports zero membership additions, removals, or renames; any delta fails.

acceptance.given: A verdict-producing validator runs against current source and emits execution evidence.

oracle.expected: The verdict record contains matching command identity, current source identity, captured process output, and exit status from the same execution.
forbidden: A verdict without an execution record.
A verdict justified only by assistant prose or static configuration.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable verdict artifact links source hash and command invocation to captured output and status.

acceptance.then: Each produced verdict is traceable to real execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Inspect the verdict artifact and fail when command, source identity, or captured execution result is absent or mismatched.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require every verdict to be assembled from a recorded live command execution bound to current source identity and captured output.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Evidence fields remain additive and backward compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: source and command identity captured -> validator executes -> output and status captured -> verdict references execution record
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A verdict is accepted only when command, source identity, output, and exit status all match one execution.

acceptance.given: The toolchain evaluator is invoked on a Windows host.

oracle.expected: Platform detection identifies Windows and the supported execution path completes without classifying Windows as unsupported.
oracle.observable: Validator output records Windows as the active platform and reports the Windows support check passed.

acceptance.then: Windows operation is accepted as supported with declared platform behavior.
acceptance.when: When the system is operated or evaluated on Windows

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the platform-support check on Windows and fail if detection, dispatch, or declaration marks Windows unsupported.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Detect Windows explicitly, route supported commands through the Windows execution adapter, and record declared platform behavior.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema migration; platform declaration remains compatible with existing evidence consumers.

slice_hint.state_transition: host platform detected -> Windows policy selected -> command executed via Windows adapter -> support result recorded
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: On Windows, the support validator records supported status and succeeds; unsupported classification fails.

acceptance.given: The requested target identity is recorded, then execution resolves to a substituted target.

oracle.expected: Independent identity verification detects the substitution and rejects or halts processing before acceptance or verdict emission.
forbidden: Accepting a substituted target as the requested target.
Treating filename-only equality as identity proof.
oracle.observable: The validation result records differing requested and resolved identities and returns a fail-closed rejection.

acceptance.then: The substituted target is not accepted and processing has failed closed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run target identity and effective-content verification with a substituted fixture and require rejection before processing continues.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Compare requested and resolved target identities plus effective inspected content; fail closed whenever substitution is detected.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; rejection behavior is additive to existing target validation.

slice_hint.state_transition: requested identity captured -> resolved target inspected -> identities compared -> substitution rejected before acceptance
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validator exits with fail-closed rejection and no accepted result whenever requested and resolved identities differ.
